name: Color grade
controls: The global color transform laid over the finished image, like the film stock it was shot on or the colorist's pass: white balance, black and white points, contrast curve, saturation, split toning and the grain or halation that comes with a stock.
question: Should the film look clean and true to color, or carry a grade, like a particular film stock or a colorist's look?
notes: Color (its own dimension) chooses the palette: which hues and in what proportions. The grade is what happens to every pixel afterwards: it shifts the white balance, lifts or crushes the blacks, rolls off the highlights, bends saturation and tints shadows and highlights. A grade matters most for photography, footage, 3D and cinematic or analog styles; for flat vector styles it reduces to black lift, contrast, saturation and texture. Pick one grade for the whole film: a grade that changes between scenes reads as a mistake unless the story motivates it (a flashback, a before/after). A coding agent cannot 'shoot on Portra 400': every film-stock or look name must be decomposed into parameters, and every option's prompt here does that. Parameters: white balance (warm or cool shift, tint toward green or magenta); black point (lift = shadows never reach 0, matte/milky; crush = shadows clamp to 0); white point and highlight roll-off (how highlights compress before white); contrast curve (S-curve strength); saturation (global and per range: shadows, skin, greens); split tone (a hue added to shadows and another to highlights); hue shifts (greens toward teal, reds toward orange); and stock artefacts (grain amount and size, halation radius and tint, gate weave, vignette). Implement a grade as one stack on the #world wrapper (or on the photo/footage layers only, see below): (1) an SVG filter with feComponentTransfer (type linear: slope and intercept set the black lift and white point; type gamma or table for the curve) and feColorMatrix (type saturate, or a matrix for channel mixing and warm/cool shifts), referenced with filter:url(#grade); or CSS filter functions for simple cases (contrast(), saturate(), brightness(), sepia(), hue-rotate()); (2) split-tone overlays: a solid dark tint in mix-blend-mode:lighten lifts the shadows toward that hue, a solid light tint in mix-blend-mode:multiply pulls the highlights toward that hue; (3) texture on top (grain, halation, vignette) from the texture and effects dimensions. Media elements can instead use HyperFrames' color-grading support for video and images. The brand wins: after grading, the logo, UI and brand accent must stay recognizable (roughly within delta-E 5 of the brand hex); if a grade pushes them off, grade only the photographic and atmospheric layers and leave UI and logo layers ungraded. Full-frame SVG filters are expensive to render: prefer grading static layers once, keep filter chains short, and test render time on a 2-second slice. Teal-orange and heavy contrast are also the default 'AI look' of generated imagery; choose them for a reason and say it.

options.what: No stylistic grade: accurate white balance, full but not clipped range, colors exactly as designed.
options.looks: True whites and neutral grays, brand colors exact, normal contrast, no tint, no grain beyond anti-banding dither.
options.motion: Nothing; the grade is invisible by design.
options.use: UI-led films, brand-exact work, data and explainers, any film where the palette is the look.
options.vs: Cool clinical is a deliberate cool, low-saturation look; clean neutral has no look at all.
options.prompt: Apply no grade: no filters on the world wrapper, no tint overlays, no vignette. Keep whites at #fafafa or the brand's white (never blown), blacks at the brand's darkest ink (never below #0a0a0a on large fields), and every brand color exactly as specified. If a large gradient bands, add 1.5-2% static noise dither, nothing more.

options.what: A strong S-curve that clamps the deep shadows to black and pushes highlights bright, for a graphic, punchy image.
options.looks: Deep solid blacks with little shadow detail, bright highlights, bold separation, saturation slightly up in the mids.
options.motion: Cuts feel harder; shapes read as silhouettes quickly.
options.use: Sport, music, bold launches, fashion, trailers, dark premium product films.
options.vs: Bleach bypass is high contrast with desaturation and a silver sheen; crushed contrast keeps or raises saturation. Overdone it becomes the over-crisp AI finish.
options.prompt: Grade with a hard S-curve: feComponentTransfer type table per channel with values '0 0 0.12 0.5 0.9 1 1' (shadows below about 15% clamp to 0, highlights above about 90% clip to 1), or CSS filter: contrast(1.25) brightness(0.98). Saturation 1.05-1.1 (feColorMatrix saturate). No black lift. Check that dark text on dark surfaces still reads; keep type out of the crushed zone.

options.what: Blacks lifted to a soft gray or tinted floor and saturation eased into pastel, for a soft, airy, printed feel.
options.looks: No true black anywhere (the darkest tone is a tinted gray), low contrast, soft pastel colors, gentle highlights.
options.motion: Everything feels softer and slower; motion reads calm.
options.use: Lifestyle, wellness, fashion, playful consumer apps, whimsical and editorial styles.
options.vs: Faded warm vintage adds a strong warm cast and grain; pastel matte is clean, lifted and cool-to-neutral.
options.prompt: Lift blacks and soften: feComponentTransfer type linear slope 0.86 intercept 0.1 on each channel (black floor at about 10%, white ceiling about 96%); saturation 0.8-0.85; optionally tint the floor with a lighten-blend solid (#2b2a3a for cool, #3a2f2b for warm) at 100% so shadows never go below it. Contrast comes from ink color and size, not the curve. No vignette, grain at most 3%.

options.what: A lab process that leaves silver in the image: high contrast, low saturation and a harsh metallic sheen.
options.looks: Desaturated colors (about half), hard contrast, bright gritty highlights, deep shadows, a cold silvery overall cast.
options.motion: Gritty and severe; hard cuts and weight suit it.
options.use: War, crime, security, industrial and heavy-hardware stories, serious or tense beats.
options.conveys: Grit, severity, tension, realism under pressure.
options.vs: Desaturated documentary is low saturation with normal or soft contrast; bleach bypass pairs low saturation with very high contrast.
options.prompt: Grade bleach bypass: feColorMatrix saturate 0.45-0.55, then a contrast curve (feComponentTransfer table '0 0.02 0.3 0.6 0.95 1') or CSS contrast(1.3); overlay a luminance copy of the image (grayscale, overlay blend, 35-50%) for the silver sheen; slight cool cast via a multiply solid #eef2f5. Grain 5-8% static or per-frame. Keep brand accents out of the grade or accept they will desaturate.

options.what: A complementary split tone: shadows and backgrounds pushed toward teal, skin and highlights toward orange.
options.looks: Warm orange highlights and skin against cool teal shadows and skies; strong color separation of subject from background.
options.motion: Blockbuster energy; pairs with big camera moves and hits.
options.use: Action-styled launches, trailers, travel, sport; only when the brief wants blockbuster.
options.conveys: Cinematic spectacle, heat against cool, Hollywood gloss.
options.vs: Mixed warm/cool lighting motivates warm and cool from real sources; teal-orange applies them globally by tone. It is the most overused grade and a known slop tell: justify it.
options.prompt: Split-tone teal and orange: a lighten-blend solid #0f3a40 (lifts shadows to teal, 100%, or 60-80% for subtlety) and a multiply-blend solid #ffe0c2 (pulls highlights to orange, 70-100%); then contrast(1.1) saturate(1.1). Optionally hue-shift greens toward teal with feColorMatrix. Keep skin or warm subjects in the orange range and backgrounds in the teal; exclude UI and logo layers if the brand is neither color. State the reason in the direction.

options.what: A gentle, non-complementary tint in shadows and a different tint in highlights, for mood without a named look.
options.looks: Barely-there color in the shadows (often cool blue or green) and warmth in the highlights; the image still reads as natural.
options.motion: Invisible as an effect; it only shapes the mood.
options.use: Brand films, editorial, storytelling where a clean grade feels too digital and teal-orange too loud.
options.vs: Teal-orange is a strong complementary push; a subtle split tone moves shadows and highlights only a few percent.
options.prompt: Split-tone subtly: a lighten-blend solid #10161f at 100% (shadows no darker than that cool floor) and a multiply-blend solid #fff4e6 at 60-80% (highlights warm by about 3-5%). Saturation 0.95, contrast 1.03. The result must still pass for neutral at a glance; brand colors shift no more than delta-E 3.

options.what: The look of slide film developed in negative chemistry: shifted, clashing hues, yellow-green highlights, blue or magenta shadows, harsh contrast.
options.looks: Oversaturated, off-kilter color, yellowish or cyan highlights, magenta-blue shadows, blown whites, high contrast.
options.motion: Loud and restless; suits fast cuts and music.
options.use: Music videos, streetwear, youth and nightlife brands, 90s and early-2000s references.
options.conveys: Rebellion, energy, lo-fi cool, retro edge.
options.vs: Kodachrome is saturated but faithful; cross-process is saturated and wrong on purpose.
options.prompt: Cross-process: feColorMatrix type matrix boosting red and green in highlights and blue in shadows, for example values '1.15 0.05 0 0 -0.02  0 1.1 0 0 0.02  0 0 0.85 0 0.08  0 0 0 1 0'; then contrast(1.25) saturate(1.3); a lighten-blend solid #1a1340 for magenta-blue shadows; highlights allowed to clip. Grain 6-10%. Never apply to UI that must stay brand-exact.

options.what: The look of a warm professional color negative stock: soft contrast, peachy skin, gentle highlights and fine grain.
options.looks: Warm white balance (+300-500K), soft lifted shadows, highlights that roll off gently instead of clipping, muted greens, fine grain.
options.motion: Human and unhurried; suits slow pushes and held moments.
options.use: Lifestyle, people-first brand films, hospitality, craft and handmade products, warm storytelling.
options.conveys: Warmth, authenticity, human touch, nostalgia without kitsch.
options.vs: Faded warm vintage is older and more degraded (strong fade, color shift); warm negative is clean, modern film.
options.prompt: Emulate a warm color negative: warm shift via feColorMatrix (R x1.04, B x0.94) or a multiply solid #fff0e0 at 60%; black lift with feComponentTransfer linear slope 0.93 intercept 0.05; highlight roll-off with a gamma of 0.95 on the top range (or table '0.05 0.3 0.58 0.8 0.93 0.97'); saturation 0.9 with greens desaturated further; fine grain 3-5%, per-frame seeded, 1px. No halation, no vignette.

options.what: The look of tungsten-balanced motion-picture film at night: cool teal-cyan shadows, warm practicals, and in its no-antihalation variant, red halos around every light.
options.looks: Cyan-teal cast in shadows and ambient light, warm sodium or tungsten practicals, clean deep shadows, visible grain, red-orange halation around bright edges and lights.
options.motion: Nocturnal, moody; neon and street-light sources glow.
options.use: Night scenes, neon noir, city and nightlife, moody product films, music.
options.vs: Day-for-night fakes night from a day image; tungsten night assumes real light sources and adds film halation.
options.prompt: Emulate tungsten night film: cool the ambient with a lighten-blend solid #0c2a33 (teal shadow floor) and feColorMatrix (B x1.06, R x0.94) on non-practical layers; keep practicals warm (#ffb36b-#ffc98a). Halation on highlights only: duplicate the bright layer, threshold it (feComponentTransfer steep table), blur 8-16px, tint #ff4a1c, screen at 25-40%. Contrast 1.08, saturation 0.95. Grain 6-9%, per-frame seeded, slightly coarse (tile scaled 1.5x).

options.what: The look of color reversal (slide) film: saturated, cool-leaning, contrasty, with clean deep blacks and crisp color.
options.looks: Clean saturated blues and greens, cool neutral balance, firm contrast, rich blacks, very fine grain, highlights that clip rather than roll off.
options.motion: Crisp and bright; suits clean cuts and graphic compositions.
options.use: Travel, outdoor, tech-meets-nature, editorial and magazine-style films, bright product worlds.
options.vs: Kodachrome leans warm with deep reds and yellows; slide film here leans cool with vivid blues and greens.
options.prompt: Emulate slide film: saturation 1.2, contrast 1.15 (table '0 0.03 0.25 0.55 0.85 1'), slight cool shift (B x1.03, R x0.98), blacks clean at 0-2% (no lift), highlights allowed to clip near white. Very fine grain 2-4%, static or per-frame. Optional mild vignette 15-20% multiply.

options.what: The look of the classic mid-century reversal stock: deep saturated reds and yellows, strong blues, dense shadows and a warm nostalgic cast.
options.looks: Rich primary reds, warm yellows, deep skies, dense contrasty shadows, slightly warm whites; no pastel softness.
options.motion: Classic and bold; pairs with steady framing and deliberate moves.
options.use: Retro and mid-century styles, Americana, food and travel, heritage brands, nostalgic stories.
options.vs: Faded warm vintage is washed out and lifted; Kodachrome is dense and saturated.
options.prompt: Emulate Kodachrome: saturation 1.25 with reds and yellows boosted further (feColorMatrix raising R and G response in warm hues), a warm cast (multiply #fff1dc at 50%), dense shadows (table '0 0.02 0.22 0.52 0.84 1', no lift), contrast 1.12. Blues kept deep, not cyan. Grain 3-5% fine. No halation.

options.what: The look of cool-leaning color negative stocks: muted greens and cyans, cool shadows, restrained saturation and soft contrast.
options.looks: Greens pushed toward cool teal-green, magenta-free skin, soft cool shadows, gentle overall desaturation, fine grain.
options.motion: Quiet and observational.
options.use: Urban and East-Asian-inspired aesthetics, calm lifestyle, architecture, thoughtful editorial films.
options.vs: Warm negative pushes peach and amber; muted green film pushes cool green and cyan.
options.prompt: Emulate a cool green negative: shift greens toward cyan-green with feColorMatrix (G x1.02, B x1.03, R x0.96), saturation 0.85, lift blacks slightly (linear slope 0.94 intercept 0.04) with a cool floor (lighten solid #14201e), highlights soft (top of table 0.95). Fine grain 3-5% per-frame. No vignette.

options.what: The look of a motion-picture release print: rich contrast, dense blacks, warm-neutral highlights that roll off smoothly and gently saturated color.
options.looks: A cinematic tone curve (smooth toe and shoulder), slightly warm highlights, deep neutral-cool shadows, rich but controlled saturation.
options.motion: Suits deliberate camera moves and longer holds; reads as 'cinema'.
options.use: Brand films, trailers, cinematic product films, anything that should feel projected.
options.vs: Warm negative is softer and brighter (a camera negative); print film is denser and more contrasty (the projected print).
options.prompt: Emulate a release print: filmic S-curve with a soft toe and shoulder (feComponentTransfer table '0 0.03 0.18 0.46 0.74 0.9 0.97'), highlights warm (multiply #fff6ea at 50%), shadows neutral-cool (lighten #0e1216), saturation 1.05, contrast via the curve only. Grain 3-5%. Optional letterbox only if the direction chose 2.39:1.

options.what: Classic black-and-white film: full tonal range from true black to paper white, strong contrast and visible grain.
options.looks: Pure grayscale, deep blacks, bright whites, strong midtone separation, visible organic grain; color only if one element is exempted.
options.motion: Timeless and serious; motion and shape carry everything.
options.use: Documentary, heritage, fashion, dramatic or historical beats, flashbacks.
options.vs: Grayscale in color treatment is a palette of flat grays; black-and-white film is a grade with grain and a film curve.
search: high contrast black and white film
options.prompt: Grade to black and white: feColorMatrix type saturate values 0 (or a luminance matrix weighting R 0.3, G 0.59, B 0.11; push the red weight up to 0.4 for brighter skin); contrast curve table '0 0.04 0.3 0.62 0.92 1'; grain 7-10% per-frame seeded, slightly coarse. Optional vignette 20-25%. The brand accent, if kept, becomes a color-key exception (see color key).

options.what: A single-hue monochrome: black and white toned toward one color, as in sepia, cyanotype blue or selenium purple-brown.
options.looks: Every tone is a shade of one hue (brown, blue, green or violet) from a dark tinted shadow to a pale tinted highlight.
options.motion: Archival and dreamlike; suits memories, history and slow transitions.
options.use: Heritage and history, flashbacks, archive-footage treatments, editorial and blueprint styles.
options.vs: Duotone grade maps shadows and highlights to two different colors; tinted monochrome uses one hue throughout.
options.prompt: Tone to one hue: desaturate fully (feColorMatrix saturate 0), then tint: a multiply-blend solid of the highlight tone (sepia #f2e3c6, cyanotype #cfe3f5) and a lighten-blend solid of the shadow tone (sepia #2e1f12, cyanotype #0b2a4a). Contrast 1.05, grain 4-8%, optional vignette 20%. Keep the tint identical across scenes.

options.what: A gradient map that renders every luminance level as a blend between two chosen colors: shadows become one hue, highlights another.
options.looks: Photos and footage reduced to two brand colors (for example deep navy shadows and coral highlights), graphic and poster-like.
options.motion: Unifies mixed footage and photos into one graphic system; the map can switch colors on a beat.
options.use: Brand films mixing many photos, music and event promos, editorial and Swiss-poster styles, making stock photos ownable.
options.conveys: Graphic boldness, brand unity, poster energy.
options.vs: Duotone in color treatment is a two-color palette for the graphics; the duotone grade maps photographic tones to two colors.
options.prompt: Map luminance to two colors: desaturate the photo layer (feColorMatrix saturate 0), then an SVG feComponentTransfer with type table per channel running from the shadow color to the highlight color (for navy #14213d to coral #ff7a59: feFuncR table '0.078 1', feFuncG '0.129 0.478', feFuncB '0.239 0.349'). Add contrast 1.1 before mapping. Apply only to photo and footage layers; type and UI stay in the palette. Switch the pair only on a downbeat, never tween between maps.

options.what: The image is black and white except for one hue (usually the brand accent or the story's key object), which stays in full color.
options.looks: A monochrome world with a single saturated element pulling the eye.
options.motion: The colored element becomes the protagonist; color can spread from it at the turn.
options.use: Isolating the product in a busy world, before/after, the one thing that matters, a turn where color floods back.
options.vs: Tinted monochrome colors everything with one hue; color key leaves everything gray except one hue.
refs: Schindler's List (the girl in the red coat)
options.prompt: Keep one hue: render the scene in black and white (saturate 0 on all layers) except the key element, which sits on its own ungraded layer in full color (the brand accent or the story object). For photos, isolate the hue with a mask of the object rather than a global hue key (draining globally then repainting fails). One key element per scene; if color floods back at the turn, reveal it with a radial clip-path from the key element over 0.6-1.0s, power2.inOut.

options.what: Turning a daylight image into night: underexposed, heavily blue, desaturated, with skies darkened and only lights left bright.
options.looks: Deep blue cast, low exposure, desaturated, darkened sky, crisp moonlit shadows, practicals added as warm points.
options.motion: Quiet, nocturnal; the reveal of lights switching on is the natural event.
options.use: Night beats built from day assets, time-passing sequences, moody turns, 'after hours' stories.
options.conveys: Night, secrecy, calm, the passage of time.
options.vs: Blue hour is a real twilight light with a glowing sky; day-for-night is a grade that darkens everything and keeps moonlit shadows.
options.prompt: Grade day-for-night: brightness 0.45-0.55, saturation 0.4-0.5, strong blue shift (feColorMatrix R x0.7, G x0.85, B x1.15, or a multiply solid #6f86c4), darken the sky or top of frame with a top-down multiply gradient (#000 at 30-45% to transparent at 50% height), contrast 1.1 so shadows stay crisp. Add warm practicals as ungraded glowing points (#ffc27a, 2-radius glow). Keep text on its own ungraded layer.

options.what: A restrained, naturalistic grade with reduced saturation and soft contrast, as in observational documentary.
options.looks: Muted natural colors (saturation 60-75%), soft contrast, neutral or slightly cool balance, real texture kept.
options.motion: Handheld or steady observational camera; nothing flashy.
options.use: Customer stories, founders and teams, social impact, B2B trust films, real footage reels.
options.vs: Bleach bypass adds harsh contrast and silver; documentary keeps contrast soft and honest.
options.prompt: Grade for documentary restraint: saturation 0.65-0.75, contrast 0.95-1.0 (slight lift: linear slope 0.96 intercept 0.02), neutral to slightly cool balance (B x1.01). Keep real footage texture; grain 2-4% only if footage is clean digital. Brand accent may stay at full saturation on graphics layers as the only saturated color.

options.what: A cold, clean, slightly desaturated grade with bright neutral-blue whites and hard-edged clarity.
options.looks: Cool whites (#f2f6fa-ish), blue-gray shadows, low saturation except for one clean accent, crisp contrast, no grain.
options.motion: Precise and controlled; suits mechanical and precise motion languages.
options.use: Health tech, biotech, security, infrastructure, precision hardware, lab and data stories.
options.vs: Clean neutral has no cast; cool clinical deliberately shifts cool and drains warmth.
options.prompt: Grade cool and clinical: cool shift (feColorMatrix R x0.95, B x1.05, or multiply #eef4ff at 70%), saturation 0.8 overall with the accent layer exempt, contrast 1.08, blacks neutral-cool (lighten #0d1218), whites near #f4f8fb. No grain, no vignette, no halation.

options.what: An aged color print: warm-yellow cast, faded lifted shadows, shifted hues and heavier grain, like a photo left in the sun.
options.looks: Yellow-orange cast, cyan faded out of the shadows, lifted milky blacks, soft contrast, muted greens and blues, visible grain, soft vignette.
options.motion: Nostalgic and slow; suits gate weave and gentle flicker.
options.use: Retro and seventies styles, memories, heritage stories, analog-feeling brand films.
options.vs: Warm negative is clean modern film; faded vintage is decades-old film that has color-shifted.
options.prompt: Grade faded vintage: warm-yellow cast (multiply #ffe7b8 at 60-80%), lifted shadows with a warm floor (lighten #3a2d1f; linear slope 0.85 intercept 0.1), saturation 0.75 with blues pushed toward teal-gray, contrast 0.92. Grain 8-12% per-frame, vignette 25-30% multiply, optional gate weave 0.3-0.8px seeded. Keep type legible: set it outside the grade or boost its weight.

options.what: An overexposed-leaning, soft, low-contrast grade with bright highlights, lifted shadows and pastel color.
options.looks: Luminous whites, soft pale shadows, gentle warm or neutral cast, low contrast, soft pastel saturation.
options.motion: Light and gentle; floaty holds without idle loops.
options.use: Wellness, beauty, wedding and lifestyle, family and education apps, soft consumer launches.
options.vs: Pastel matte lifts blacks but keeps midtones; bright and airy lifts the whole exposure toward white.
options.prompt: Grade bright and airy: brightness 1.06-1.1, shadows lifted (linear slope 0.88 intercept 0.1), contrast 0.9, saturation 0.85, slight warm cast (multiply #fff8ef at 60%). Keep whites below clipping on large areas (max #fbfaf8). No vignette, grain at most 2%. Check text contrast: use a dark ink, never gray on white.

options.what: The color of consumer analog or early digital video: bleeding chroma, hot highlights, crushed shadows and slight color shifts.
options.looks: Smeared, offset color edges, oversaturated reds, blooming hot highlights, low sharpness, slight green or magenta cast, scanlines or tracking noise optional.
options.motion: Handheld, zooms, date stamps; the grade carries the era.
options.use: 90s and home-video references, nostalgia, music, youth culture, 'found footage' devices.
options.vs: The VHS texture option is the surface artifact (tracking lines, noise); the video tape grade is the color response. Use both for the full look.
options.prompt: Grade like tape: chroma bleed by offsetting a red-channel copy 2-4px right and a blue copy 1-2px left (feColorMatrix channel isolation plus feOffset, screen), soften with 0.6-1px blur, saturation 1.15 with reds hottest, highlights blooming (bright-pass blur 6-10px, screen 25%), shadows crushed (table '0 0 0.2 0.55 0.9 1'), slight green cast (G x1.02). Add the texture dimension's VHS or scanlines layer for artifacts. Keep essential text on an ungraded layer.
